issues.legal_issue: A later judgment setting aside parts of a development notification does not affect completed or ongoing construction undertaken under the notification while it was in force and pursuant to duly sanctioned plans.
material_facts: The construction plans were sanctioned under an amendment that reduced the restricted coastal setback while that amendment remained in force.
The projects had been initiated during the period between the amendment and the later judgment, after obtaining the required clearances from the relevant agencies.
The earlier judgment invalidated two parts of the amendment but did not direct demolition of existing structures or specify that ongoing construction would be affected.
The earlier judgment's reasoning addressed the amendment's allowance of new construction, and the authorities responsible for implementing the coastal rules interpreted it as prospective.
issues.conclusion: The earlier judgment does not affect completed or ongoing construction undertaken pursuant to plans sanctioned under the amendment before the relevant parts of that amendment were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment must be read as a whole and in the context of the issues and facts before the court, not as if it were a statute. Whether a judgment operates retrospectively or prospectively depends on the text and context of the decision and a balance of relevant considerations, including reliance on the previous legal position, public interest, the purpose of the rule, and the consequences of retrospective operation. The Court relied on Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India, (1996) 5 SCC 281, and Managing Director, ECIL, Hyderabad v. B. Karunakar, (1993) 4 SCC 727. The relevant regulatory framework included Rule 5(d) of the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986, and the 1991 Coastal Regulation Zone Notification as amended in 1994.

rule.if: construction_effect_proceeding and plans_sanctioned_under_then_effective_relaxation and project_initiated_before_relaxation_was_invalidated and required_clearances_obtained and earlier_judgment_did_not_direct_destruction_or_retroactive_effect

predicates.construction_effect_proceeding: The proceeding asks whether an earlier court judgment affects construction undertaken under a development rule that was later invalidated in part.
predicates.plans_sanctioned_under_then_effective_re: The competent authorities sanctioned the construction plans under a relaxation that was in force when they acted.
predicates.project_initiated_before_relaxation_was_: The project was initiated before the relevant relaxation was invalidated by the later judgment.
predicates.required_clearances_obtained: The project obtained the clearances required from the relevant agencies before it was initiated.
predicates.earlier_judgment_did_not_direct_destruct: The earlier judgment neither directed destruction of existing construction nor stated that it would operate retrospectively against construction already undertaken.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns the effect of a later judgment on construction begun under a then-effective relaxation with required clearances, and that judgment did not direct destruction or retrospective effect, the construction is not affected by that judgment.

issues.legal_issue: A coastal management authority may decide the merits of a referred construction matter when a court has directed it to consider the matter and that direction has attained finality.
material_facts: A High Court directed the national coastal management authority to consider the matter referred to it by the Ministry and to report after hearing the concerned parties.
The authority considered the matter and issued its decision.
The parties challenging that decision had not challenged the High Court's direction before a higher forum.
issues.conclusion: The contention that the authority should instead have directed the parties to approach the High Court was rejected because the authority reconsidered the matter pursuant to an unchallenged order that had attained finality.
issues.legal_principle: A direction requiring an authority to consider a matter and report, if left unchallenged and allowed to attain finality, cannot be avoided by later arguing that the authority should have sent the parties back to court. The judgment relies on the procedural history and finality of the High Court's direction.

rule.if: authority_decision_proceeding and court_referred_matter_to_authority_for_consideration and referral_order_unchallenged and authority_considered_referred_matter

predicates.authority_decision_proceeding: The proceeding challenges a decision made by an authority on a referred matter.
predicates.court_referred_matter_to_authority_for_c: A court directed the authority to consider the matter and report on it.
predicates.referral_order_unchallenged: The parties did not challenge the court's referral direction before a higher forum, and it attained finality.
predicates.authority_considered_referred_matter: The authority considered the matter referred to it.

issues.definition: If a court finally directs an authority to consider a matter and the authority does so, its decision is not invalid merely because the parties could have been sent back to court.

issues.legal_issue: An interpretation protecting qualifying coastal construction applies to comparable cases generally when the competent authority has determined that the clarification is not limited to the particular applicants.
material_facts: The national coastal management authority concluded that the Ministry's clarification was correct and consistent with the coastal notification.
The authority stated that the clarification applied to comparable cases in coastal areas throughout the country.
The respondents argued that granting the applicants the benefit of the interpretation would unfairly deny it to others.
issues.conclusion: The argument that the petition should be dismissed because the applicants alone had been favoured was rejected; the clarification applied to comparable cases throughout the country's coastal areas.
issues.legal_principle: A claim that an interpretation selectively benefits particular applicants has no force where the competent authority has expressly determined that the clarification applies to all comparable cases. The judgment relied on the authority's recorded conclusion concerning the scope of the clarification.

predicates.selective_benefit_challenge_proceeding: The proceeding includes a claim that an interpretation benefits only the applicants and should therefore not be applied in their case.
predicates.competent_authority_endorsed_interpretat: The competent authority concluded that the interpretation was correct and consistent with the applicable regulatory framework.
predicates.authority_said_interpretation_applies_to: The authority stated that the interpretation applies to comparable cases beyond the particular applicants.

issues.definition: A claim of selective benefit is rejected when the competent authority endorses the interpretation and states that it applies broadly to comparable cases.
